verses.text: "I'm worn out by my life. I'll speak my complaint freely and let the bitterness in my soul come out.
I'll say to God, 'Don't condemn me. Show me why you have a case against me.
Does it please you to oppress me, despise what your own hands made, and smile on the plans of the wicked?
Do you have human eyes? Do you see things the way people do?
Are your days as short as a mortal's, or your years like a human lifetime,
that you have to hunt for my guilt and search for my sin?
You know I'm not wicked, yet no one can rescue me from your hand.
Your hands shaped and made every part of me, and now you're destroying me.
Please remember that you shaped me like clay. Will you turn me back into dust?
Didn't you pour me out like milk and let me thicken like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and tendons.
You gave me life and showed me faithful love, and your care kept my spirit alive.
Yet you kept these things hidden in your heart. I know this was in your mind:
if I sinned, you'd take note of it and refuse to clear me of my guilt.
If I'm wicked, I'm doomed. Even if I'm right, I can't lift my head. I'm full of disgrace and all too aware of my suffering.
If I hold my head high, you hunt me like a lion and show your power against me again.
You bring fresh witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me. Wave after wave of trouble comes at me like troops in battle.
Why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I'd breathed my last before anyone saw me.
It would have been as though I'd never existed, carried straight from the womb to the grave.
Aren't my days few? Stop and leave me alone so I can have a little comfort
before I go where I can't return, to the land of darkness and the shadow of death,
a land dark as midnight, where the shadow of death covers everything and nothing has order, where even the light is like midnight.'"
